papers.abstract_en: In multi-agent debates, matching reports can arise for two different reasons: agents may repeat the same evidence (replication), or they may provide separate evidential roots that support the same claim (corroboration). A judge must distinguish these two cases. Counting report occurrences gives extra weight to relays, paraphrases, alias resubmissions, and excerpt splits, while merging all matching content avoids this only by also removing genuine corroboration. We formalize this tension as a minimal judgment game in which acquiring new evidence is costly, but replication is cheap. We show that root replication invariance (RRI) is exactly threshold-uniform replication immunity. Under RRI, replication-only deviations cannot change the verdict, and positive-cost replication is strictly dominated, whereas occurrence-sensitive and content-keyed judges admit profitable deviations. We also establish an information boundary: if a judge's observation interface cannot distinguish a replica from a matched fresh root, no judge can both ignore the replica and respond strictly to the fresh root. To preserve this distinction, we introduce the lineage quotient, which removes wording, identity, occurrence multiplicity, and arbitrary root names while keeping distinct roots separate. On orbit-connected domains, it is the coarsest representation sufficient for every deterministic judge invariant to replication and root-label renaming. We further lift this construction to quantitative bipolar argumentation frameworks (QBAFs), characterize strict fresh-root response, prove its propagation along sign-consistent paths under DF-QuAD, and derive a tight closed-form response modulus. Exhaustive audits over 28,224 direct-star profiles, 2,052 multi-layer DAGs, with matched interventions on 277 AVeriTeC-derived profiles, show the predicted separation between replication and corroboration under a supplied partition.

papers.abstract_en: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

papers.abstract_en: Owners of data in cloud object storage cannot directly check whether the provider still keeps every object unchanged. Existing research mostly checks blocks inside files or relies on third-party auditors, and less attention has been given to checking each object against a public blockchain reference while measuring the cost. A full-data audit downloads every object and compares it with a saved hash list, which is slow and only as reliable as that list. We propose a public auditing system in which the SHA-256 hash of each object and its name forms a leaf of a Merkle tree, so the whole dataset is represented by one Merkle root. This root is stored in an Ethereum smart contract as a trusted public record, while the objects stay with the provider. An auditor downloads an object, rebuilds the root using a short Merkle proof and compares it with the stored root, marking the object as intact, modified or missing. In five experiments on an S3-compatible store and a local Hardhat blockchain (normal audit, single- and multiple-object tampering, deletion and scalability), the system detected 15 of 15 single modifications, 2,205 of 2,205 modified objects and 830 of 830 deleted objects with no false alarms. The proof needed only 14 hashes for 10,000 objects, so checking one object took about 10 ms and a 100-object sample about 150 ms regardless of dataset size, while a full audit of 10,000 objects (14.3 s) took about as long as downloading them (13.5 s). Storing the root cost 91,863 gas, 252 times less than storing 1,000 hashes on-chain. The system thus shows exactly which objects were modified or are missing, with its main savings coming from checking selected objects.

papers.abstract_en: In a recent paper~\cite{BGW}, Bizoń, Glogić, and Wasserman (BGW) reduced the classification of smooth self-similar Yang--Mills profiles in odd spatial dimensions $d\ge11$ to an algebraic problem of counting roots of an explicit polynomial in a prescribed interval. Two roots correspond to explicit profiles. BGW conjectured that there is exactly one additional root and verified this in a range of odd dimensions. Here, we prove the existence of an additional root, and hence of a third smooth self-similar profile, in every odd dimension $d\geq11$. The proof combines an endpoint sign calculation for the resonance polynomial with an algebraic argument showing that the third root is distinct from the two explicit ones. Uniqueness remains open in general.

We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of $\mathcal{M}_M$. Finally we show that $\partial \mathcal{M}_M$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

papers.abstract_en: We study the $p$-adic valuation trees associated with the sequence \[ e_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}F_n(t)\,dt, \] obtained by evaluating the Laplace transforms of the Fibonacci polynomials at $1$. We answer an open question of Givens and Moll in the negative by constructing an explicit counterexample showing that even internal branches need not be simple. We then reformulate the Givens--Moll lifting criteria for the even and odd subsequences in terms of the roots and derivatives of two associated polynomials. In particular, simple roots modulo $p$ give rise to simple internal branches. Finally, we develop a recursive lifting procedure that determines the unique surviving residue class at each level of a branch associated with a simple root and computes the $p$-adic valuations of the corresponding terms.

papers.abstract_en: We establish asymptotic results for profile score statistics under sequences of parameters that may tend to the boundary of the parameter set. When the likelihood is profiled over a set with boundary points, the distribution of the statistic can depend, even asymptotically, on a distance to the boundary that cannot be estimated consistently. We address this in three ways. First, we give conditions under which the nuisance score has a root on an extended parameter set, and the profile score statistic formed with that root converges to a chi-squared distribution. Second, we show that the efficient score statistic converges to a chi-squared distribution under a separate condition that can hold even for estimators constrained to the original set. Both lead to confidence regions with asymptotically correct coverage probability, uniformly on sets that may contain boundary points, and the conditions allow the scores for the interest and nuisance parameters to grow at different rates or become asymptotically collinear. Third, we quantify the coverage error of applying the profile score statistic without an extended set. We approximate the distribution of the statistic and bound the error by a quantity that decays like a normal tail in the standardized distance to the boundary. The approximation also gives one-sided tests with least favorable critical values whose asymptotic size is at most the nominal level. We illustrate the results in a zero-inflated Poisson model and a one-way random effects model.

papers.abstract_en: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether this design beats letting a capable model investigate on its own. We compare three simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent and the Codex coding agent) with five published LLM RCA agents and with statistical and causal methods on RCAtlas, 90 validated cases from eight public datasets, across six models and three reasoning efforts. The simple harnesses are the most accurate (PR@1 65-77% on three mid-tier models), ahead of the published agents (16-53%) and the non-LLM methods (6-39%), on every model on which both families were run. The published agents fix from a tenth to all of their model calls in the program, and a case study shows how these prescriptions skip the decisive evidence. A stronger model mainly improves reliability, a multi-turn harness mainly improves aptitude, and more reasoning effort changes accuracy by a few points at most while multiplying the time by up to seven. Among runs more accurate than the best non-LLM method, every Pareto-optimal run in cost or time uses a simple harness.

papers.abstract_en: We prove accelerated mixing for a Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin sampler: the OBABO splitting with friction $2\sqrt m$, adjusted with Neal's non-reversibly updated uniform, which is redrawn after every epoch of $E$ steps. For targets $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $mI\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq LI$ and an $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian, started from a Gaussian at an approximate minimizer, the chain reaches total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ after $\tilde O\big(\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}(d/m)^{3/4}\big)$ gradient evaluations, where $κ=L/m$ and $\tilde O$ hides logarithmic factors. The $\sqrtκ$ term is necessary, already on Gaussian targets. The proof discretizes Lu's entropic hypocoercivity by means of an entropy inequality for free transport, so that the relative entropy of the unadjusted chain decays at a rate of order $\sqrt m$ up to a discretization bias. papers.abstract_en: Bivariate random-effects models are commonly used to jointly synthesize sensitivity and specificity in diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) meta-analysis. However, existing approaches may be sensitive to distributional assumptions and may produce biased estimates of accuracy and between-study heterogeneity with sparse meta-analytic data. We proposed a novel bivariate structural equation modelling (BSEM) approach for DTA meta-analysis and evaluated its performance relative to the bivariate linear mixed model (BLMM) and bivariate generalized linear mixed model (BGLMM). We conducted extensive simulations under varying study, sample-size, accuracy, and heterogeneity conditions. We assessed model performance using bias, root mean squared error (RMSE), confidence interval width, empirical 95% coverage probability (CP), and convergence. We generated study-specific random effects from bivariate normal, t, and Laplace distributions to assess robustness to distributional misspecification. We also applied the models to two empirical DTA datasets. The BSEM generally produced smaller bias and RMSE and nominal-level CP for pooled sensitivity and specificity than the BLMM, while the BGLMM generally yielded results between the two approaches. The BLMM showed stable convergence but tended to underestimate between-study heterogeneity. We observed similar performance patterns under the three random-effects distributions. In the empirical applications, differences between model estimates were generally consistent with patterns observed in the simulations. Overall, the proposed BSEM provided a flexible alternative approach for jointly modelling sensitivity and specificity in DTA meta-analysis, with performance that was generally favourable relative to the BLMM and comparable to the BGLMM across the simulated and empirical settings considered.

papers.abstract_en: Cytokine-mediated inflammation disorders such as sepsis and cytokine release syndrome demand bedside multiplex panels that resolve pro- and anti-inflammatory dynamics in minutes, yet label-free FET cytokine sensors remain limited to few devices, single analytes, and PDMS packaging that sorbs small molecules and leaches oligomers. We present a CMOS platform pairing a 128 x 128 ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) array (SkyWater 130 nm, SiN gate) with a FlexDym 4 x 1 micro-well overlay that partitions the membrane into four chemically independent regions (approximately 2,176 pixels each, square-root-of-N averaging). Two wells carry capture antibodies (anti-IL-6, anti-IL-10), one is a non-specific reference, and one tests specificity; the transduced signal is defined as the differential current relative to the reference signal (Delta I_D(W_n) - Delta I_D(W_3)). Single-analyte dose-response measurements spanning 100 fM to 10 nM successfully resolve both IL-6 and IL-10 above the non-specific detection floor, including at healthy-serum baseline concentrations. The array shows a per-pixel pH sensitivity of 1.13 microamperes per pH unit (CV approximately 14%). Across two chips, device-to-device variation is dominated by transconductance spread (g_m CV approximately 62%); a one-time per-device g_m calibration reduces analyte-measurement variance to approximately 16%. We further validate the surface functionalization, characterize device-to-device variation, and demonstrate the FlexDym integration workflow. Simultaneous multiplexed cytokine measurements resolve IL-6 (W1) and IL-10 (W2) against the chemistry-only reference (W3). At the same time, cross-specificity characterization is assessed by applying IL-6 to an anti-IL-10 well (W4), establishing a scalable label-free ISFET architecture for multiplexed cytokine sensing.

papers.abstract_en: Reconstructing a radio map (RM) from sparse received-power measurements supports non-cooperative interference monitoring and spectrum management. However,sparse measurements leave uncertainty about both the global RM and the interfering emitter location, making informative sampling and accurate reconstruction challenging. To address these challenges, a novel joint sampling and reconstruction method named RMSampler is proposed in this paper to improve measurement selection and RM reconstruction under limited measurement budgets. For measurement selection, RMSampler evaluates global RM error reduction using the covariance of diffusion-generated RMs and localization error reduction using candidate emitter locations. Because these errors have different units, their expected relative reductions are combined into a scale-invariant sampling criterion, with each acquired measurement updating both uncertainty estimates. After sampling, the updated emitter-location probabilities guide a separate conditional diffusion ensemble for final reconstruction. To improve measurement agreement, an effective sample size (ESS) target guides robust posterior correction, followed by a minimum-distortion projection enforcing measurement and building constraints. For the reconstruction ensemble, analysis establishes that increasing likelihood power reduces expected robust measurement loss, while pretrained neural parameters and architecture remain unchanged. Experiments using simulated and real-world measured data demonstrate improved reconstruction under matched measurement budgets. In the Chongqing real-world measured data experiment, root mean square error (RMSE) decreases from 3.54 to 2.73~dB relative to random sampling under a common reconstruction method.

For two-factor matrix representations wider than both output dimensions, with individually full-row-rank factors, we classify all admissible joint ranks: closure occurs precisely at effective scalar-balanced minimal joint rank or a two-value signed spectral family at full joint rank. All intermediate ranks are excluded; positive represented flows belong to known square-root families. For general representations with constant ambient representation and gradient-Lie ranks, ordinary closure is equivalent to a local invariant-level metric in the analytic case and specified smooth regimes. An endpoint section forces the initially unrestricted mobility map to admit a locally smooth representative on the represented image. We also separate testing families: linear losses locally admit closure at every submersion, whereas one fixed translated strongly convex quadratic family fails it on a delayed-bracket example. A fixed output readout gives an ordinary squared-loss witness. These supporting results do not characterize quadratic-only closure in general. We retain the unresolved smooth output-rank-two case with Lie rank at least four. A frozen deterministic experiment checks a separate engineered-loss construction; it is distinguished from the squared-loss proof, universal theorems and empirical learning performance.

papers.abstract_en: We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.

papers.abstract_en: Rapid and accurate hypocenter determination based on three-dimensional (3D) seismic velocity models is essential for seismic monitoring in subduction zones, yet it remains computationally demanding. HypoNet Nankai, a hypocenter determination package that uses physics-informed neural network (PINN) travel-time inference for a realistic 3D P-wave velocity model of the Nankai Trough subduction zone, was designed to address this problem, but supported only P-wave arrival times. Here, we present HypoNet Nankai PS, which extends the framework to both P- and S-wave travel times. We first constructed an S-wave velocity model from the existing P-wave model using empirical conversion relations for marine sediments and the crust. Because the resulting S-wave velocity structure has lower velocities and therefore considerably steeper travel-time gradients, the original PINN training procedure designed for the P-wave velocity structure was insufficient. We therefore revised the training procedure by reconsidering the distribution of collocation points, the NN architecture, and the optimizer. Benchmark comparisons with the fast marching method showed that the revised approach substantially reduced the root-mean-square deviations for both P- and S-waves compared with the original algorithm. Recovery tests using synthetic earthquakes were also performed. When applied to 223 earthquakes recorded by DONET stations off the Kii Peninsula, the system yielded hypocenters generally consistent with the JMA catalog beneath the network, suggesting that the 3D velocity model captures travel-time variations accommodated by JMA's 1D model and station corrections. Farther seaward, the estimated hypocenters were substantially shallower than those in the JMA catalog and were located in the oceanic crust and uppermost mantle, consistent with previous relocations that used DONET data and 3D velocity models.
